rationale: The Court is likely to affirm on an Andrews/Dillon-style threshold rule: Congress’s nonretroactive § 924(c) amendment cannot itself supply the “extraordinary and compelling” gateway, though resulting disparity may be considered only after some independent extraordinary circumstance opens the door and then under § 3553(a). A Kagan-led dissent (possibly joined by Sotomayor and Jackson, with some chance of separate writing) will stress the negative-implication from “rehabilitation alone” and read Concepcion to permit consideration of intervening legal changes within § 3582(c)(1)(A)’s individualized discretion.
